title: Partner pricing bundle mapping and privacy Q&A (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working draft to align partner pricing bundles (how we map Redwood product SKUs to marketplace SKUs), and to capture fast answers to privacy/KMS/data-residency questions that marketplace reviewers and partners will ask during onboarding. Intended for GTM, Partner Ops, Legal (initial review), and Solutions Engineering.

TL;DR summary:
- We need a compact SKU mapping matrix (hosted API, dedicated capacity, private on-prem license) plus two bundle flavors for marketplace tiles: developer-trial and enterprise-commit.
- Each marketplace (AWS, Azure, GCP) has slightly different billing/sku constraints and privacy disclosures; prepare tailored copy and a one-page privacy appendix per marketplace.
- Target acceptance criteria: tile copy + screenshots, billing SKU mapping, short privacy Q&A, test tenant with sample invoices.

Current constraints / assumptions (fast notes):
- Hosted API = metered per-token pricing (primary); marketplace meters may not support per-token microbilling directly so we will expose monthly packages or units (e.g., 100K token credits as SKU).
- Dedicated = reserved GPU capacity; map to time-block SKUs (vGPU-month equivalents) for marketplaces that only support usage-based charges through marketplace metering APIs.
- Private = subscription/license + support; in some marketplaces this must be a private offer or bring-your-own-license (BYOL).

Mapping checklist (work items):
- Define canonical Redwood SKUs and canonical names (owner: Priya).
  - redwood-hosted-credits-100k
  - redwood-hosted-credits-500k
  - redwood-dedicated-1gpus-month
  - redwood-private-license-annual
- For each SKU, define: token-equivalent, list price (USD), suggested marketplace SKU format, billing type (one-time vs recurring vs usage meter).
- For hosted per-token -> marketplace credit bundles: choose round numbers that map cleanly to price tiers and waterfall to discounts (e.g., 100k credits, 500k, 2M).
- For Dedicated -> map to monthly reservation SKUs; coordinate with SRE to define minimal provisioning unit.
- For Private -> create BYOL SKU that references a procurement contract and support SKU.

Marketplace-specific notes:
- AWS Marketplace:
  - Supports metering (API-based usage) but requires an AMI or SaaS integration depending on deployment. SaaS metering can accept usage records; confirm token-to-meter translation with engineering (Ethan).
  - Private offers and negotiated terms supported; we must be ready with a CSV of SKU rates and invoice samples.
  - GDPR/privacy: provide data flow diagram and indicate whether customer data traverses Redwood control plane (yes for hosted), plus options for VPC/e2e KMS.
- Azure Marketplace:
  - Tends to prefer monthly or recurring SKUs; usage-based offerings require telemetry pipeline integration.
  - For Dedicated, recommend offering both a marketplace-recurring and direct-managed contract to support enterprise SLAs.
  - KMS integration: list supported key providers and whether we can support customer-managed keys for hosted variant.
- GCP Marketplace:
  - Supports SaaS metering but onboarding can be slower; recommend initially listing credit bundles and a follow-up metered offer if demand justifies.
  - Data residency: GCP reviewers often request region mapping; prepare an authoritative list of regions and where requests are processed.

Privacy & KMS Q&A (short answers for partner-facing PR/FAQ):
- Q: Does Redwood store customer prompts or outputs?
  - A: By default, hosted API request metadata and short-term logs are retained for 30 days for billing and debugging; customers on Dedicated or Private can opt-out of telemetry and logs.
- Q: Can partners require customer-managed keys?
  - A: Yes for Private deployments (on-prem/VPC) and for Dedicated we offer an optional KMS integration for encryption at rest. Hosted customers can use our managed keys today; roadmap includes tenant-customer managed keys (ETA H2 2025).
- Q: Where is inference executed?
  - A: Hosted: region-selected Redwood clusters; Dedicated: customer-dedicated GPU pools in specified region; Private: on-prem or customer cloud under their control.
- Q: What PII obligations should partners include in tile copy?
  - A: Do not claim data residency guarantees for hosted unless the customer buys Private or Dedicated with region-pinning. Instead: "Customer data is isolated per-tenant; private deployment options available for strict residency controls."

Tile copy variants (short blurbs we can A/B test):
- Developer trial (50–70 chars): "Ship LLM features fast — 100K free credit trial, pay-as-you-go."
- Startup bundle (60–90 chars): "Predictable costs for scale: reserved inference instances + developer credits."
- Enterprise commit (70–120 chars): "SLA-backed dedicated GPUs, private deployment options, and PCI/ISO-ready controls."

Acceptance criteria (what marketplace review needs to see):
- Final tile headline, short and long descriptions, and 3 screenshots (Console onboarding, billing sample, and model selection).
- SKU CSV matching marketplace template with price, currency, billing cadence, and SKU ids.
- Privacy appendix (one-page PDF) with data flow bullet points, KMS options, retention policy, and contact for security review.
- Test tenant with a sandbox invoice demonstrating the SKU mapping.

Open questions / decision items (explicit):
- Do we launch metered SaaS offers simultaneously across AWS/Azure/GCP or stagger? (Implication: engineering integration effort per marketplace; recommend staggered with AWS first.)
- Billing translation: who on finance signs off on token-to-credit conversion rates? (Action: Finance lead to approve by 2024-11-18.)
- Legal: confirm private offer language for BYOL contract (Legal owner: Marina).

Next steps / owners:
- Priya: finalize canonical SKU names and initial price tiers (due 2024-11-12).
- Ethan: confirm metering API feasibility for AWS SaaS metering and provide a mapping doc (due 2024-11-22).
- Marina: draft the one-page privacy appendix and BYOL contract boilerplate (due 2024-12-01).
- Diego: create tile creative variants and gather screenshots (due 2024-12-05).

Notes to self / scratch area (informal):
- Might be simpler to present hosted credits as "compute credits" rather than tokens for marketplace UX — less technical for procurement.
- Need a short line for tile: "Optimized inference runtime, pay for what you use." Might be too generic.
- Flag: GCP legal often asks for explicit subprocessors list — compile from infra team.

Appendix (links for collaborators):
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-1254 (marketplace go-to-market checklist)
- Jira: JIRA-GTM-402 (marketplace SKU mapping epic)
- GitHub: marketplace-assets PR #78 (sample CSV and tile images)

Unresolved / parking lot items:
- Currency conversion strategy for EU/GB customers across marketplaces.
- How taxes & VAT are represented in the SKU display and invoices.

If anyone is reviewing: add comments inline in Google Drive doc. This is intentionally rough — focus on getting the SKU matrix and privacy appendix to the review-ready state first.
